svg.title: Locks & Deadlocks
svg.desc: Locks & Deadlocks. Row locks make writers wait for each other; two transactions waiting on each other is a deadlock, and the database aborts one. Step 1, One open transaction: A forgets to COMMIT: B and C queue for order 497003, then A's next UPDATE closes a cycle. Step 2, Row locks and the queue: The row lock is xmax in the row: B waits on A's xid, C on the tuple lock, and readers don't wait. Step 3, Detect, abort, prevent: After deadlock_timeout (1 s) A is aborted with 40P01; sorted locks, timeouts and SKIP LOCKED help. Step 4, Schema changes and InnoDB: A waiting ALTER TABLE queues every read behind it; InnoDB detects deadlocks at once and locks gaps.

g.text: A forgets to COMMIT: B and C queue for order 497003, then A's next UPDATE closes a cycle.
The row lock is xmax in the row: B waits on A's xid, C on the tuple lock, and readers don't wait.
After deadlock_timeout (1 s) A is aborted with 40P01; sorted locks, timeouts and SKIP LOCKED help.
A waiting ALTER TABLE queues every read behind it; InnoDB detects deadlocks at once and locks gaps.
BEGIN; UPDATE orders SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE id = 497003;
… then idle in transaction: no COMMIT
UPDATE orders SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE id = 499846;
BEGIN; UPDATE orders SET status = 'shipped' WHERE id = 499846;
UPDATE orders SET status = 'shipped' WHERE id = 497003;
UPDATE orders SET shipping_country = 'TH' WHERE id = 497003;
SELECT id, status FROM orders WHERE id = 497003;
not blocked: it reads the committed row
ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN gift_note text;
after 7.0 s, almost all of it waiting
SELECT id, status FROM orders WHERE id = 497001;
SELECT id, status FROM orders WHERE id = 497003;
SESSIONS · ONE RUN ON A LAPTOP · POSTGRESQL 18.6
SESSIONS · A SCHEMA CHANGE, ANOTHER RUN
ROW LOCKS · WHO WAITS FOR WHOM
A waits for B, and B waits for A
row lock = xmax in the row: A’s xid
check finds the cycle: A aborted
its locks go; B, then C, get row 497003
A JOB QUEUE · FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
SELECT id FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid'
ORDER BY id LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED;
A 4th packer used NOWAIT instead: ERROR 55P03 at 497001, at once
TABLE LOCKS ON orders · pg_locks AT 5 s
COMMIT at 8 s releases the lock
shop-app and support wait for deploy, not for the report:
a waiting ACCESS EXCLUSIVE request blocks every request behind it
Fix: SET lock_timeout = '2s' first. The ALTER gave up after 2.0 s (55P03),
reads waited 1.0 s at most, and the retry after the report took 2.6 ms
The culprit does nothing: idle in transaction, still holding
its row lock. The two writers wait on a lock, not on CPU or I/O.
at 20.5 s: its transactionid and tuple rows
DETAIL: Process 14562 waits for ShareLock on
Process 14564 waits for ShareLock on transaction
HINT: See server log for query details.
CONTEXT: while updating tuple (2194,90) in relation "orders"
A rolls back; its UPDATE of 497003 is undone. Retry the whole transaction.
more runs on the same data
for A, 5 ms after it closed the cycle
innodb_deadlock_detect = ON: found at once, no timer to wait out
REPEATABLE READ: next-key locks on all 27 entries, and the gaps
customer 1051: 10 ms. PostgreSQL has no gap locks: both took under 8 ms
